rationale_summary: Innovation enablement is the dominant frame because the guideline, issued under Japan's AI Promotion Act, explicitly rejects rigid single standards in favor of voluntary, agile, risk-based governance designed to promote social implementation, lower adoption barriers, foster high-quality data ecosystems, and maximize AI benefits through leading public-sector utilization. Fundamental rights is the strongest runner-up—anchoring the guideline's core 'human-centricity' principles in human dignity, fundamental human rights, fairness/non-discrimination, and privacy—but these principles are consistently framed as guardrails that enable trustworthy adoption and innovation rather than as the sole overarching mandate. Consumer and public safety (preventing physical harm, fraud, crime, deepfake abuse, and system failures) and social stability (containing misinformation and disinformation) form substantial secondary rationales, alongside economic competitiveness (growth, fair competition, corporate advantage, and global leadership via the Hiroshima AI Process), while national security and labor transition appear only briefly in risk lists and skills guidance.

evidence_spans.quote: AI contributes to economic growth and the advancement of peopleʼs lives and it is important to promote its social implementation and innovation.

Furthermore, to reduce barriers to AI adoption in various contexts, with regard to issues that can be anticipated or that may arise when utilizing AI, the government will organize the issues and ideas regarding the interpretation and application of where responsibility lies, and strive to clarify interpretations as much as possible based on precedents, etc.
Respecting human dignity and fundamental human rights, and complying with the laws and regulations
Identifying and evaluating the risks of illegal activities such as various crimes including cyberattacks and fraud perpetrated through the misuse of AI, and implementing appropriate measures.

In particular, given that the spread of misinformation and disinformation generated by AI poses a serious risk, R&D institutes and utilization business operators will strive to develop technologies that can determine whether something is generated by AI (digital watermarks, provenance management, APIs19, etc.) and will implement them as necessary.
Proactively disclosing and explaining these initiatives is expected to enhance corporate value and secure competitive advantage.
